lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach compound leaves, 5-part flowers, nectar-disc/gland architecture and strongly lobed/segmented fruits across three dryland project genera.

project_scope.note: The project pool spans three very different Zygophyllaceae habits: woody guayacan, prostrate/herbaceous Kallstroemia, and resinous creosote bush.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Look for usually compound leaves with stipules on a dryland herb/shrub/tree, then inspect a 4–5-part flower with a conspicuous nectar-disc/gland system and a superior ovary that is often strongly lobed or partitioned.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Herbs, shrubs or trees, often xerophytic; leaves usually opposite or alternate and compound—2-foliolate to pinnate—often with persistent or spine-like stipules.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers bisexual, usually radial and 5-merous; petals free; stamens commonly 10 or otherwise equal/twice petal number; nectar glands or disc conspicuous. Ovary superior and often deeply lobed or multi-locular.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Variable but characteristically segmented/lobed in project genera: capsules in Guaiacum, multi-mericarpy in Kallstroemia, and a lobed hairy schizocarp/capsular fruit in Larrea.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Dryland plant + compound leaves/stipules + 5-part flower + obvious gland/disc + strongly lobed or segmented fruit is the Zygophyllaceae package.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: compound leaf/stipules → 5-part flower/disc → ovary lobing → three genus doors → Krameriaceae comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Zygophyllaceae is best learned by fruit and leaf architecture. The three project genera look very different until you notice the compound leaves, floral glands and strongly partitioned fruits.

steps.title: 1 · Larrea door: two resinous leaflets
steps.look_for: Opposite leaves divided into two small resinous leaflets, strong odor/resin, and yellow 5-petal flowers.
steps.why_it_matters: The 2-foliolate leaf is a fast dryland genus clue.

steps.title: 2 · Follow Larrea to the hairy 5-part fruit
steps.look_for: A densely hairy, 5-lobed fruit derived from a 5-carpellate ovary.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit reveals the family’s strongly partitioned gynoecium.

steps.title: 3 · Kallstroemia door: prostrate herb + 10-part fruit
steps.look_for: Opposite pinnate leaves, yellow/orange flowers, and a 10-lobed fruit breaking into multiple one-seeded units.

steps.title: 4 · Guaiacum door: woody blue-flowered member
steps.look_for: Woody shrub/tree with pinnate leaves, blue-purple 4–5-petal flowers, 8–10 stamens and a lobed capsule.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows the woody extreme of the family while retaining the lobed-ovary/fruit pattern.

steps.title: 5 · Find the nectar glands/disc
steps.look_for: Glandular structures at or near stamen bases surrounding the ovary.
steps.why_it_matters: This connects otherwise dissimilar genera at the flower level.

comparisons.title: Zygophyllaceae vs Krameriaceae
comparisons.rule: Both are Zygophyllales. Zygophyllaceae project flowers are mostly radial with conventional petals/stamens and multi-carpellate segmented fruits; Krameriaceae is zygomorphic, hemiparasitic, has two oil-secreting petals and a one-seeded spiny fruit.

comparisons.title: Zygophyllaceae vs Fabaceae
comparisons.rule: Compound leaves overlap, but Zygophyllaceae lacks legume pods and commonly has radial 5-part flowers with nectar glands/discs and multi-part capsules/schizocarps.

visual_lesson.caveat: No single leaf arrangement is universal. Fruit architecture and flower-center glands are safer than leaf form alone.

genera.fast_cue: resinous shrub + opposite 2-foliolate leaves + yellow flower + hairy 5-part fruit
prostrate/ascending herb + pinnate leaves + yellow/orange flower + 10-lobed schizocarp
woody pinnate leaves + blue-purple flower + lobed capsule
